transcript.text: From what you have described, the most likely cause is a blocked or iced-up defrost drain. Is the freezer still cold while the fridge is warm, and is there a thick block of ice on the back wall inside the freezer?
yes freezer still freezing. fridge warm. theres a thick layer of frost on the back wall of the freezer yes
From what you have described, the most likely cause is the automatic defrost system. Behind the rear panel inside the freezer, are the coils a solid block of ice, or fairly clear?
cant take the back panel off, no idea how and dont want to break the clips. just see thick frost on the back wall

The first step is a full manual defrost: switch it off at the socket, move the food into cool bags, put towels down and leave the doors open until every bit of ice has melted, then dry it and switch it back on. Have you been able to do a full defrost, or is there no ice to clear?
no not done a full defrost yet. can do it, got somewhere for the food. how long should i leave it

You should leave the fridge-freezer unplugged for at least 24 hours to ensure all ice melts completely. This duration allows the defrost system to reset properly and prevents immediate re-icing once power is restored. Cold air comes in through vents, often on the back wall inside. Make sure food isn't pressed against them and the shelves aren't packed so tight air can't move. Were the vents blocked or was it over-packed (and have you moved things), or was everything clear?
not blocked. moved the food away from the back anyway, no difference. hardly any cold air from the slots at the back of the fridge
When you press the freezer door switch, do you hear the fan running, and are the coils clear or iced up?
can hear a faint scraping/ticking from the freezer sometimes. cant see the coils, panel's still on. just thick frost on the back wall

Ice in the bottom often means the defrost water can't drain away. At the bottom of the back wall there's a small drain hole — once the ice has melted, clear it gently with warm water or a soft pipe cleaner. Was the drain hole blocked (and is it clear now), is it still blocked or frozen, or was it already clear?
havent defrosted yet so not looked at any drain hole. dont know where it is. no burning smell or tripping btw
Run it as normal with the doors shut for a few days. Has the frost started to build up again, or is it staying clear?
